spec.title: codkit PROP-015: The Codkit runtime - the library of features and flags delivered into the own layer of a product

status.comment: the runtime library, its delivery (runtime load|check), the feature scaffolds (gen feature|brand); decisions of 2026-09-07

purpose.title: 1. Purpose and the form of delivery

p.RT-PURPOSE: The Codkit runtime is a TypeScript library in the spirit and the style of VS Code, shared by every fork Codkit maintains: a feature-flags service built on ports and adapters with observables, a host that creates a feature when its flag turns on and disposes it when the flag turns off, a message branding engine, a simulator of the remote flag source and an inspector. It exists so that the delta of a product is built as a parallel system (services through DI, contributions through registries) rather than as a set of patches, and so that every new feature of a product is isolated in its own directory and switched on by a flag (owner rulings of 2026-09-07).

facts.RT-IS-A-MANAGED-COPY: The library is delivered into a product as a **managed copy**, like the standards package: `codkit runtime load` copies the version directory from toolRoot into `<patchesDir>/delta/own/codkit/`, and a plain `codkit load` carries it on into `<tree>/src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/`; the copy is compared with the shipped version byte for byte; an edit in place is drift; an update arrives only with a new version of Codkit (`RT-LOAD-UPGRADE`).
facts.RT-DIRECTORY-IS-CODKIT: The directory of the library in the own layer is called `codkit/` (not `kit/`, not `lib/`): the name states the owner of the code unambiguously and matches the prefix of the licence scope (PROP-014 §4a `STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS`). The internal identifiers of the library (service decorators, the ids of contributions, of commands and of storage keys) live in the `codkit` namespace; the identifiers of the features, the settings and the context keys of a product carry the prefix of the product and are set by its declarations.
facts.RT-SHIPPED-LOCATION: In toolRoot the library lives in `codkit/runtime/v<semver>/`, exactly one version directory (as in `STD-PACKAGE-LOCATION`); the directory is listed in the `files` of `package.json` and travels in the tarball. The content of the version directory is exactly the tree that lands in `delta/own/codkit/` (without the notice file, which belongs to PROP-014 §4a).
facts.RT-VERSION-LITERAL: The version of the library is the directory name `v<semver>` and the literal `export const CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERSION = '<semver>';` in `common/version.ts`; a divergence is `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`. The same file holds `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM: readonly string[]`, the upstream tags on which the library has been compiled and verified.
facts.RT-ONLY-TS-AND-MD: The library consists only of `.ts` and `.md` files: no JSON, no TOML, no images, no `.license` companions - so that it requires from a product neither a build resource allow-list nor hygiene exceptions for foreign extensions; the data lives in TypeScript modules. There are no characters outside ASCII in the code and in the strings (the upstream minifier rejects non-ASCII in its output); Cyrillic is admissible only in the comments of the header.
facts.RT-EVERY-FILE-CARRIES-THE-BANNER: Every file of the library carries a licence carrier per PROP-014 §2: the four notice lines (the copyright, the English and the Russian links to UPL, `SPDX-License-Identifier: UPL-1.0`) in the comment style of its own extension (`//` for `.ts`, `<!-- -->` for `.md`) in the first lines of the file. The shipped directory passes `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` with zero problems: this is checked by `shippedRuntime.test.ts` in `npm run floor` and by the licence gate of `runtime load` before any write.
facts.RT-NO-PRODUCT-NAMES: The library carries the name of no product; the examples in the comments and in the tests use neutral identifiers (`acme.sample`).

purpose.fence: codkit/runtime/v0.1.0/ README.md what it is, the version, "do not edit", the licence EN/RU LAYERS.md the permitted imports per directory = the content of the product's code-import-patterns block common/version.ts CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERSION, CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM common/features/featureDescriptor.ts FeatureId, IFeatureDescriptor, IFeatureSettingDeclaration, validateFeatureDescriptor common/features/flagLayers.ts FlagLayer, FLAG_LAYER_PRECEDENCE, FlagReading, FeatureState, resolveFeature common/features/flagSource.ts IFlagSource common/features/remoteFlags.ts RemoteFlagsSnapshot, IRemoteFlagsProvider, IRemoteFlagsSimulator, parseRemoteFlagsSnapshot common/features/featureFlagsService.ts IFeatureFlagsService, FeatureExplanation common/features/featureFlagsServiceBase.ts FeatureFlagsServiceBase common/features/featureDeclarations.ts FeatureDeclarations, featureDeclarations common/features/featureHost.ts FeatureHost common/brand/brandRules.ts IBrandRule, createBrandTransform, affectedEntries browser/featureFlags.contribution.ts registerSingleton + registerAction2 + host contribution (side effects) browser/browserFeatureFlagsService.ts BrowserFeatureFlagsService browser/featureRegistry.ts registerFeature browser/featuresHost.contribution.ts FeaturesHostContribution browser/adapters/*.ts configurationFlagSource, productFlagSource, remoteFlagSource, storageRemoteFlagsProvider, contextKeyPublisher, hostRestart browser/inspector/featureFlagsInspector.ts InspectFeatureFlagsAction test/common/*.test.ts, test/browser/*.test.ts

facts.RT-PORTS-AND-ADAPTERS: The core of the library (`common/`) depends only on its own ports: the flag source (`IFlagSource`), the provider of the remote snapshot (`IRemoteFlagsProvider`), the context-key publisher, the host restart port and the factory of feature instances. The adapters to the upstream APIs lie in one directory, `browser/adapters/`, and implement the ports over the current APIs; a change of an upstream API changes one adapter, and neither the core nor the features of a product are touched. For processes without a DI registry and without context keys there are null adapters.
facts.RT-NARROW-UPSTREAM-SURFACE: The surface of contact with upstream is narrow and enforced: `common/**` imports only `vs/base/common/**`, `vs/platform/*/common/**` and its own; `browser/**` imports additionally `vs/workbench/common/contributions.js`, `vs/workbench/services/host/browser/host.js`, `vs/workbench/services/lifecycle/common/lifecycle.js`, `vs/platform/*/common/**`; nothing is imported from `vs/workbench/contrib/**`. The same list is the content of `LAYERS.md` and of the `code-import-patterns` block a product installs for the target `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/~`; `shippedRuntime.test.ts` checks the imports of the library with regular expressions over the specifiers.
facts.RT-OBSERVABLES-ARE-THE-REACTIVE-PRIMITIV: The state of a flag is an observable (`observableValue`/`derived` from `vs/base/common/observable.js`), not only an event: `enablement(id)` and `liveState(id)` return `IObservable<FeatureState>`, the host subscribes through `autorun`, and the context key is updated from that same observable; the event `onDidChangeEnablement` remains an adapter for code without observables. This is the current reactive rule of upstream (the instruction `.github/instructions/observables.instructions.md`, hundreds of files with `autorun`/`derived`).
facts.RT-FLAG-LAYERS: The flag sources form layers with the fixed precedence `FLAG_LAYER_PRECEDENCE`: `build` (the build value from `product.json` through the `descriptor.product` function) → `policy` (the `inspect().policyValue` of the setting) → `remote-force` (the forcing key of the remote snapshot) → `user` (the first defined of `applicationValue`, `userValue`, `userLocalValue`, `userRemoteValue`) → `remote-default` (the default key of the remote snapshot) → `default` (`descriptor.default`). The build value is cancelled by no other layer: security features stay a property of the build that way.
facts.RT-RESOLUTION: `resolveFeature(descriptor, readings)` returns `{ enabled, decidedBy }`: the first defined reading in the order of precedence; the `default` layer is always defined. The function is pure and is covered by a table of tests over every layer.
facts.RT-TRANSACTION-PER-CHANGE: Every event of a source (a setting change, a new remote snapshot) recomputes the affected features and applies the result in one `transaction()`: observers see no intermediate states; `onDidChangeEnablement` fires once with the list of the ids that actually changed; context keys are published only for the ones that changed.
facts.RT-COLD-FEATURES: A feature with `hotToggle: false` (a "cold" one) reads `enablement(id)` frozen at its first computation in this session; `liveState(id)` changes meanwhile, `restartPending` holds the ids of every cold feature whose live state differs from the frozen one, and the restart port shows a "Restart" notification once per such change, in the upstream idiom (`INotificationService.prompt` + `IHostService.restart()`).
facts.RT-REMOTE-IS-A-PORT: The remote source is the same kind of port as any other: `IRemoteFlagsProvider` yields the current snapshot `RemoteFlagsSnapshot { version: 1, force, defaults, issuedAt? }` and the event of its change; `parseRemoteFlagsSnapshot` parses the text strictly (version 1, boolean values, string keys) and on any error returns `undefined`, never throwing. The library contains no network code; a future server implements the port over a shared-process channel.
facts.RT-SIMULATOR: The simulator of the remote source is `StorageRemoteFlagsProvider`: the snapshot is kept in `IStorageService` (`StorageScope.APPLICATION`, `StorageTarget.MACHINE`, the key `codkit.features.remoteSnapshot`), is changed by the `simulate(patch)` and `clear()` methods of the `IRemoteFlagsSimulator` port (a `null` value in the patch removes the key) and notifies through `onDidChangeValue`. The internal switching interface and the future server thus walk one and the same path: snapshot → transaction → observables → features and `when`.
facts.RT-INSPECTOR: The inspector is `InspectFeatureFlagsAction` (id `codkit.features.inspect`, title `Feature Flags: Inspect`, `f1: true`): a Quick Pick with one line per feature (the state icon, the title, the id, the layer that decided the state, the values by layer, the status of the instance, `restart pending`); selecting a feature opens the actions - enable/disable/reset the user setting (`updateValue(…, ConfigurationTarget.USER)`), simulate a remote `force`/`default` on/off/clear, clear the simulated snapshot. Every string goes through `localize`.
facts.RT-FEATURE-IS-AN-INSTANCE: A feature of a product is an ordinary VS Code class: `extends Disposable`, dependencies through the constructor by DI, and everything the feature adds (commands, menus, views, listeners) registered in `this._register(...)`. **Enabling a feature = creating the instance through `IInstantiationService.createInstance(ctor)`, disabling it = `dispose()`.** There is no base class with a mandatory `activate`: it would call a method of the subclass from the constructor of the base class, before the parameter properties of the subclass are assigned.
facts.RT-FEATURE-HOST: `FeatureHost` (common) holds an `autorun` over `enablement(descriptor.id)`: on → it creates the instance with the factory, off → it calls `dispose()` on the instance; `dispose()` of the host destroys the instance; `state: IObservable<'inactive' | 'active' | 'failed'>`. `FeaturesHostContribution` (browser) is the only workbench contribution of the library (`registerWorkbenchContribution2('codkit.features.host', …, WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore)`): for every declaration it waits for that declaration's phase through `ILifecycleService.when(phase)` (as the upstream registry of contributions does) and creates a `FeatureHost` with the factory `ctor => instantiationService.createInstance(ctor)`.
facts.RT-FEATURE-FAILURE-IS-CONTAINED: An exception from the constructor of a feature does not bring the workbench down: the host catches it, moves the feature to `failed`, writes an `ILogService.error` and creates no instance; the inspector shows the status. The errors of the library itself are not thrown at runtime (a snapshot with an error is ignored, a missing value is `undefined`); the only exceptions are programming errors at registration (`RT-REGISTER-FEATURE`) and an unknown id in `enablement`/`liveState`/`explain`.
facts.RT-REGISTER-FEATURE: `registerFeature(descriptor, ctor, phase = WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored)` (browser) is called while the contribution module of a product is evaluated: `validateFeatureDescriptor` (a violation is a `throw`: an error of the author, caught by a test of the product before any UI); `featureDeclarations.declare({ descriptor, ctor, phase })` (a duplicate id is a `throw`); if there is a `descriptor.setting` and the build does not force the value (`descriptor.product?.(product)` is undefined, where `product` is the static import of `vs/platform/product/common/product.js`, the upstream idiom), then `registerConfiguration` with the node `{ id: setting.id, properties: { [setting.id]: { type: 'boolean', default: descriptor.default, description: setting.description, scope: setting.scope ?? ConfigurationScope.APPLICATION, tags: setting.tags, policy: setting.policy } } }`. A feature forced by the build registers no setting at all.
facts.RT-DESCRIPTOR: `IFeatureDescriptor { id, title, default, hotToggle, setting?, product?, remote? }`; `id` has the form `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*(\.[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)+$` (two parts or more - the prefix of the product is mandatory by the form); `setting: { id, description, scope?, tags?, policy? }`, where `description` is already localized by the product; `product` is a function of `IProductConfiguration` (the type is extended by the product through augmentation), not a string key: type-safe and without `any`; `remote.key` is the key in the remote snapshot, defaulting to `id`.
facts.RT-CONTEXT-KEYS: For every declaration the context key `<id>.enabled` (boolean) is published through `IContextKeyService.createKey`; it follows `enablement(id)`, so that the `when` expressions of the menus, the commands and the views of a product react to the flag without any code.
facts.RT-BRAND-ENGINE: `createBrandTransform(rules)` returns the pure function `message => message`: the rules `{ find, replace, except? }` are applied in order, `find` is a literal (no RegExp), and a rule is skipped when the message contains any string from `except`; the fast path is that no `find` occurs in the message; the results are cached in an `LRUCache` (2048). `affectedEntries(transform, entries)` returns the keys of the messages the transform changes - for the guard snapshot of a product. The module is pure (`common`, only `vs/base/common/map.js`): a product puts the hook into `_format` (`nls.ts`), which is evaluated in every process, including bootstrap; the hook itself is a patch of the product of type `hook`, and the library does not touch `nls.ts`.
facts.RT-NO-GLOBALS: The library creates no global names and does not read `globalThis` (the upstream rule "Do not introduce new types or values to the global namespace"); the only module singletons are `featureDeclarations` and the service decorator, as in the upstream registries.

testing.title: 3. The typecheck harness and the tests

facts.RT-TYPECHECK-HARNESS: The library is compiled against the upstream sources on the pin by the TypeScript of the fork itself: a mirror directory where `src/vs/*` are symbolic links into the fork tree, `src/typings` and `src/vscode-dts` are links, `node_modules` is a link, and the `tsconfig` inherits the `src/tsconfig.base.json` of the fork and includes only the own directory with the library; `tsc --noEmit` → 0. The harness is a procedure of the central session and of the second pass of a product; it is not part of the Codkit `npm run floor` (there are no upstream sources in the repository). The result is recorded in the report of the campaign and in `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM`.
facts.RT-CONTRACT-TESTS: The library carries tests in the upstream style (`suite`/`test`, `ensureNoDisposablesAreLeakedInTestSuite`, `assert.deepStrictEqual` snapshots) for its own behavior and **for its assumptions about upstream**: the last registration in a `ServiceCollection` wins; `included: false` removes a property from the configuration registry; `affectsConfiguration` fires on the setting key of a feature. A red contract test on a new pin names the assumption that broke.
facts.RT-TESTS-RUN-IN-THE-FORK: The tests of the library are compiled by the harness but are **executed only in the fork tree** after `runtime load` and `load` (the upstream `test/unit/node` and electron runners find `test/**/*.test.js` under the own directory themselves; `codkit ci --profile build` runs the node runner over the glob `vs/<own>/**/test/**/*.test.js`, which covers `codkit/test/` as well). They are not run in the Codkit vitest: upstream stubs would be a second, false upstream. The limitation is recorded in the campaign as deferred to the second pass of a product.
facts.RT-SHIPPED-RUNTIME-TEST: `codkit/test/unit/shippedRuntime.test.ts` in `npm run floor`: exactly one version directory; the version literal equals the name of the directory; only `.ts`/`.md`; the four header lines in every file; `checkLicenseCarriers` → 0 problems; the imports per `RT-NARROW-UPSTREAM-SURFACE`; no product names; no non-ASCII outside the comments of the header.

commands.title: 4. The `runtime load|check` commands; delivered files in `verify`, `save`, `inventory`

facts.RT-LOAD-STEPS: `codkit runtime load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` (patchesDir only, the tree is not read): (1) the source is the single version directory in toolRoot and the version literal (`RT-VERSION-LITERAL`; otherwise `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`, exit 2); (2) the licence gate is `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` over the version directory with the policy of Codkit → 0 problems, otherwise `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE` with the list, exit 2 and not a single write; (3) the target `delta/own/codkit/` without the notice file: `absent` / `identical` / `drift` by a comparison of the trees; a `drift` without `--upgrade` is `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with the paths, exit 1 and not a single write; (4) `--dry-run` prints the plan (the created/replaced/removed paths) and exits 0; (5) the directory is written into a temporary directory and renamed as a whole, and the notice file in the target is preserved; (6) the notice goes into both roots per PROP-014 §4a (`STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-NOTICE`, the block of components); (7) the report `{ command: 'runtime load', version, target, state: 'created' | 'upgraded' | 'unchanged', files: { written, removed }, notice }` and three hints: the graft `import '../codkit/browser/featureFlags.contribution.js';` in the composition root of the product, the `code-import-patterns` block per `LAYERS.md`, and the first feature through `codkit gen feature`.
facts.RT-LOAD-UPGRADE: `--upgrade` replaces the directory as a whole without comparing it with the previous version (Codkit keeps no old versions and does not merge): it prints the list of the removed and the replaced paths; without the flag any drift is a refusal, so edits to what was delivered are lost only by an explicit decision.
facts.RT-CHECK: `codkit runtime check` is read-only: `identical` → 0; `absent` → 0 with the text `runtime not installed`; `drift` → `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with the paths, exit 1; plus the state of the copies of the notice per PROP-014 §4a. `--json`: `data: {target:{state, version, paths}, noticeFiles}` - the same key as `standards check` has (PROP-007 §25 `CMD-RUNTIME-CHECK`).
facts.RT-DELIVERED-NOT-OWN: The files under `delta/own/codkit/**` are delivered by Codkit (PROP-005 `OWN-DELIVERED-BY-CODKIT`): they are not covered by units and do not count as code of the product; `verify` compares the installed copy with the shipped version (`CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` on a difference) and rejects an own unit with a root inside `codkit/` (`CK-E-OWN-UNDER-CODKIT`).
facts.RT-SAVE-REFUSES-DELIVERED-EDITS: `save` refuses with `CK-E-DELIVERED-EDIT` and a list when a file of the tree under `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/**` differs from `delta/own/codkit/**` or is absent from the delta; nothing is mirrored. Hint: change it in Codkit and run `runtime load --upgrade`.
facts.RT-INVENTORY-ENTRY: The inventory shows the installed library as one synthetic entry `CK-codkit-runtime` (layer `own`, category `delivered`, a `reason` carrying the version), not as files.
facts.RT-PUBLISH-KEEPS-THE-RUNTIME: The release branch of `publish` carries the files of the library: each of them carries its own header, and the condition of UPL is satisfied; only the notice file is excluded (PROP-014 §4a `STD-NOTICE-RELEASE-EXCLUSION`).

facts.GEN-FEATURE: `codkit gen feature <id> --title <text> [--setting] [--cold] [--holder <h>] [--license <spdx>] [--year <y>] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]`: the id has the form of `RT-DESCRIPTOR` (otherwise `CK-E-GEN-ID`, exit 2); the directory of the feature is the last segment of the id; it writes `delta/own/contrib/<name>/common/<name>.ts` (the id constants and, with `--setting`, the id of the setting), `delta/own/contrib/<name>/browser/<name>.contribution.ts` (a class `extends Disposable` with a DI constructor and a `registerFeature({...}, <Class>)` call; with `--cold`, `hotToggle: false`; the description of the setting through `localize`), `delta/own/contrib/<name>/test/browser/<name>.test.ts` (a skeleton with `ensureNoDisposablesAreLeakedInTestSuite`; the test lies in the directory of the feature - `GEN-TEST-LIVES-WITH-THE-FEATURE`); at the end it prints the import line for the composition root of the product and a reminder to declare the unit in `patchset.delta.json`.
facts.GEN-BRAND: `codkit gen brand [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` (the header is as in `gen feature`, `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`) writes `delta/own/common/brand.ts` - a starter table of rules with one example and a comment about the exceptions, exporting `brandMessage = createBrandTransform(RULES)` - and prints the text of the hook for `_format` in `nls.ts` with two reminders: the hook is a patch of the product of type `hook`; the target `src/vs/{monaco.d.ts,nls.ts}` in `code-import-patterns` must permit `vs/<ownDirName>/common/~`.
facts.GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS: The generated files are code of the product: the header is written from `--holder`/`--license` (the year is `--year` or the current one) in one of two styles. `--header-style line` (the default) is four `//` lines: the copyright first, the SPDX last. `--header-style block` is a block comment of the upstream shape: the line `/*---…---`, ` * Copyright (c) <year> <holder>. All rights reserved.`, ` * Licensed under the <license> licence. The full licence text is the licence file of this repository.`, ` * SPDX-License-Identifier: <license>`, the line ` *---…---*/` - so that the own code of a product looks like the upstream code next to it (`MI-SAME-SHAPE-AS-UPSTREAMS-PARALLEL-SYSTEM`). `--header-file <path>` (a path relative to patchesDir) writes the header verbatim from a file of the product - for shapes that the fields cannot express; the file must end with a line break; it does not combine with `--holder`/`--license`/`--year`/`--header-style` - exit 2, nothing written. `--header-style` without `--holder`/`--license` is exit 2 (there is nothing to shape). Without the header flags the files are written with no header and with the warning `no header written; pass --holder and --license, or --header-file`. The header of Codkit is never written into the files of a product.
facts.GEN-TEST-LIVES-WITH-THE-FEATURE: The test of the skeleton lies inside the directory of the feature (`delta/own/contrib/<name>/test/browser/`) and not in a common `delta/own/test/`: a unit of the own manifest owns its own tests, and the declaration of the single unit `delta/own/contrib/<name>` covers both the code and the test; the runners of the fork find it by the glob `vs/<ownDirName>/**/test/browser/**` (PROP-010 `TESTS-LAYER-SPLIT`). The reminder at the end of the command names only that unit.
facts.GEN-REFUSES-EXISTING: If at least one target file exists - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS` with the path, exit 1, nothing written.

facts.RT-COMPAT-DECLARATION: `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM` lists the upstream tags on which the current version of the library has been compiled by the harness and has passed its tests; `runtime load` prints a warning when the pin of the product (`codkit.json` `pin.tag`) is not in the list.
facts.RT-SEMVER: The API of the library towards the features of a product (`registerFeature`, `IFeatureFlagsService`, `IFeatureDescriptor`, `createBrandTransform`) is versioned semantically; a breaking change is a new major version, and `runtime load --upgrade` across a major prints a warning with the list of changes from the `README.md` of the library.
facts.RT-CYCLE-GATE: The upgrade cycle (`codkit cycle`) on a new pin first of all compiles the installed library and runs its tests in the fork tree; a red result names the file of the adapter and the assumption. The rule is written down; the implementation is the next campaign.

p.DECISION-RT-MANAGED-COPY:
**Decision:** the library is delivered as a managed copy under the control of Codkit rather than generated once.
**Why:** three products with three diverged editions of the flags service is exactly what the owner wanted to avoid; the mechanism of delivered own files already exists (`LICENSE-CODKIT.md`).
**Considered and rejected:** - "generate and forget" (`flags gen` literally) - the fixes never reach the products; - a vibe package - it does not deliver TypeScript into `src/`; - writing the service in every product - duplication and divergence.
**When to revisit:** if products start editing the delivered files more often than once per cycle - then part of the library moves into generated skeletons.

p.DECISION-RT-NAME-CODKIT:
**Decision:** the directory `codkit/`, and the identifiers of the library in the `codkit` namespace.
**Why:** `kit` is a common word and may collide with a directory of the product; `codkit` names the owner and matches the prefix of the licence scope.
**Considered and rejected:** `kit/`, `lib/`, `vendor/`.
**When to revisit:** not planned.

p.DECISION-RT-PORTS-AND-ADAPTERS:
**Decision:** the core on its own ports, the adapters to upstream in one directory, a narrow surface of imports enforced by the linter; no detection of the shape of an upstream API at runtime.
**Why:** over the 814 commits since the pin the registries of DI, of contributions and of configuration did not change, but the history knows a replacement of an API (`registerWorkbenchContribution` → `registerWorkbenchContribution2`); an adapter turns such a replacement into an edit of one file; a breakage must be loud at compilation, not silent at runtime.
**Considered and rejected:** `if ('x' in service)` and duck typing - a silent degradation; `any` - forbidden by the rules of upstream; copies of upstream classes "for robustness" - a second upstream.
**When to revisit:** when upstream rewrites DI or the model of configuration - a new set of adapters with the API towards the features unchanged.

p.DECISION-RT-FEATURE-IS-AN-INSTANCE:
**Decision:** a feature is an instance of `Disposable` that the host creates through DI when the flag turns on and disposes when it turns off; one host contribution for all the features, with the phases through `ILifecycleService.when`.
**Why:** this is the life cycle of upstream itself; a base class with `activate()` called from an `autorun` in its own constructor would call a method of the subclass before the parameter properties of that subclass are assigned (they are assigned after `super()`), that is, it would fail on the first feature with injection.
**Considered and rejected:** `abstract class FeatureContribution` with `activate(store)` - a trap of construction order; `queueMicrotask` - it hides the order; `registerWorkbenchContribution2` per feature with a dynamic subclass - parameter decorators are not allowed on a class expression, and the registry accepts only a constructor.
**When to revisit:** if upstream gives the registry of contributions a factory with arguments.

p.DECISION-RT-OBSERVABLES:
**Decision:** the state of a flag is an observable; the event remains an adapter.
**Why:** the rule of upstream (the instruction `observables.instructions.md`, `autorun`/`derived` in hundreds of files); `transaction()` gives a snapshot without intermediate states; upstream does not recommend events for control flow.
**Considered and rejected:** `Emitter`/`Event` alone - no transactions and no derivation.
**When to revisit:** when the reactive primitive of upstream changes.

p.DECISION-RT-REMOTE-LAYERS:
**Decision:** the remote source gives two layers - the forcing one (a kill switch) above the user and the default one below it; the build outranks them all.
**Why:** a server has two different intents - to switch a broken feature off for everyone, and to set the default of a rollout; upstream has the layer "the default of a setting arrives from the server" (`experiment` in the schema of a setting → `IWorkbenchAssignmentService.getTreatment` → `registerDefaultConfigurations(source: 'experiments')`), which confirms the shape of the default layer; upstream has no forcing layer, other than policy.
**Considered and rejected:** a single remote layer without a mode - it either breaks the choice of the user or cannot switch a feature off.
**When to revisit:** when a real server appears - to decide whether the default layer goes through an own implementation of the upstream assignment service.

p.DECISION-RT-SIMULATOR-IN-STORAGE:
**Decision:** the simulator of the remote source keeps the snapshot in `IStorageService` and is edited by the inspector.
**Why:** it works in desktop and in web, requires no watcher and no file path, and walks the same port as the future server.
**Considered and rejected:** a file under user data with a correlated watcher - absent in web, extra code.
**When to revisit:** if the snapshot has to be replaced from outside the process (then a shared-process channel, as for the server).

p.DECISION-RT-STATIC-PRODUCT-AT-REGISTRATI:
**Decision:** forcing by the build is checked at the evaluation of the module through the static import of the product; the setting is either registered or not.
**Why:** registering the schema of a setting is an action of the module-evaluation moment (the upstream idiom); DI is not available at that moment; at that same moment the upstream `src/main.ts` and `server.main.ts` read the static `product` as well.
**Considered and rejected:** `included: false` - an empty entry in the registry; `configure({ prefix })` before the imports - imports are hoisted and the order is not guaranteed.
**When to revisit:** if upstream stops exporting the static `product`.

p.DECISION-RT-UPGRADE-FLAG:
**Decision:** a version update is `--upgrade`, which replaces the directory as a whole; without the flag any drift is a refusal.
**Why:** Codkit keeps no past versions, so "an edit of the product" cannot be told from "an old version"; the explicit flag makes the loss of edits deliberate.
**Considered and rejected:** a three-way merge - there is no base; an automatic replacement - it loses edits silently.
**When to revisit:** if Codkit starts keeping a manifest of the hashes of past versions.

p.DECISION-RT-TESTS-IN-FORK:
**Decision:** the tests of the library are compiled by the harness and executed in the fork tree.
**Why:** there are no upstream sources in the Codkit repository; stubs would be a second, false upstream.
**Considered and rejected:** vitest with mocks of `vs/*`; building a mini upstream in a fixture.
**When to revisit:** if Codkit gets a polygon with a fork tree in CI.

p.DECISION-RT-ONLY-TS-AND-MD:
**Decision:** the library has no resources and no data outside TypeScript and Markdown.
**Why:** the hygiene of the fork: unknown extensions fall under the checks of indentation and of the header; resources require entries in two allow-lists of the build; `.license` companions are yet another unknown extension; data in TS is the upstream idiom (`codiconsLibrary.ts`).
**Considered and rejected:** `compat.json`/`RUNTIME.toml` for the version - they are not needed, the version is read from the literal.
**When to revisit:** if the library needs a binary resource.
